raw.quick_summary: The model describes a damped oscillation: x(t)=A·exp(-βt)·cos(ωt). The cosine term controls oscillation frequency, while the exponential envelope controls how quickly the amplitude decays. With A=1 and ω=3 fixed, increasing β from 0.1 to 0.5 makes the oscillation lose amplitude much faster.

key_concepts.explanation: The displacement is modeled by x(t)=A·exp(-βt)·cos(ωt).
A sets the initial amplitude scale; here A=1.
β is a nonnegative decay rate. Larger β causes the amplitude envelope to decrease more rapidly.
ω controls the oscillation rate through the cosine factor. Here ω=3 and is held fixed when comparing decay rates.
The envelope is A·exp(-βt), which bounds the magnitude of the oscillation and decreases over time.
The simplified model treats β and ω as independent teaching parameters and does not model critical damping.

steps.title: Read the displacement model
steps.learning_goal: Identify the roles of the factors in x(t)=A·exp(-βt)·cos(ωt).
steps.explanation: The displacement combines an exponential decay factor with a cosine oscillation. A sets the initial scale, β controls decay, and ω controls oscillation rate.
steps.connection_to_previous: This establishes the full model before separating its effects.

steps.title: Interpret the envelope
steps.learning_goal: Use A·exp(-βt) to understand amplitude loss.
steps.explanation: The envelope gives the maximum magnitude scale of the oscillation. Because β is nonnegative, the envelope decreases or stays constant; larger β makes it fall faster.
steps.connection_to_previous: Once the equation is identified, the exponential factor explains how the amplitude changes over time.

steps.title: Hold the frequency fixed
steps.learning_goal: Recognize what remains unchanged in the requested comparison.
steps.explanation: With ω=3 fixed, both cases oscillate at the same angular frequency. Changing β affects the envelope, not the cosine frequency, in this teaching model.
steps.connection_to_previous: This separates the effect of decay from the independent effect of oscillation rate.

steps.title: Compare β=0.1 and β=0.5
steps.learning_goal: Predict which oscillator loses amplitude faster over 0 to 8 seconds.
steps.explanation: The β=0.1 case has envelope exp(-0.1t), while β=0.5 has envelope exp(-0.5t). Therefore β=0.5 produces substantially faster amplitude decay, even though both cases share A=1 and ω=3.
steps.connection_to_previous: The comparison follows directly from using the envelope while keeping the frequency fixed.

steps.title: State the model limitation
steps.explanation: This model treats β and ω as independent teaching parameters and does not represent critical damping or classify damping regimes.
steps.connection_to_previous: After interpreting the numerical comparison, this clarifies what conclusions the model does and does not support.
